However, according to our cohort study that selectively screened patients aged >70 years with carotid bruit, history of cerebrovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, or peripheral vascular disease before coronary artery bypass surgery, reducing the screening load by 40% had minimal impact on surgical management or neurological outcomes.

While selective screening in this specific context may have reduced the number of unnecessary tests and procedures, it's not universally applicable. Other factors such as individual patient risk profiles, comorbidities, and clinical guidelines would need to be considered when determining whether a screening test is necessary for carotid artery stenosis before coronary artery bypass surgery.

It's essential to note that this study had specific population parameters (age >70, history of cerebrovascular disease or diabetes), which may not be applicable in all cases. Therefore, it's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional for personalized advice on assessing and managing carotid artery stenosis before coronary artery bypass surgery.
